sections.h2: What does the Montgomery County Register of Deeds handle?
sections.html:
This office files the paper trail of land ownership in Montgomery County: deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats, releases and the index that ties them together. The county's department page calls it the legal custodian of real estate and vital records.

The staff also handle veterans' discharge records (DD 214), assumed name and partnership filings, and UCC fixture filings. Residents go there for marriage licenses and certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates, and newly commissioned notaries take their oath there.

A seller in Troy, Biscoe, Candor, Star or Mount Gilead meets this office at the very end of a sale. A buyer's title examiner searches its index before closing, and the new deed lands in its books afterward. A quick cash sale follows the same route as any other.

sections.h2: How large is Montgomery County, and what is a typical house worth?
sections.html:
Montgomery County is a small, rural county in the Uwharrie region, home to an estimated 26,403 people in mid-2025. Its 491.54 square miles of land work out to roughly 52 residents for each square mile, and the 2020 headcount of 25,751 was lower than the 27,798 counted in 2010.

The housing numbers below describe who the typical seller is and what the typical house is worth.

sections.h2: Who owes the excise tax at a Montgomery County closing?
sections.html:
That falls on the seller. Under the statute, whoever transfers the property hands the tax to the county's land records office ahead of recording (G.S. 105-228.30).

The levy is $1.00 on each $500 block of value, and a partial block is counted as a whole one. Half of every payment stays in county hands and the other half goes to the State.

  • Your closing attorney normally carries the payment with the deed.
  • If a parcel spans two counties, the county with more of its value collects.
  • Ask the attorney for the final amount before signing, since it tracks the value stated on the deed.

sections.h2: What do recording fees look like in Montgomery County?
sections.html:
No local price list exists here. G.S. 161-10 sets a single schedule for every register of deeds, calls it complete and exclusive, and requires payment before filing.

  • An ordinary deed is priced by page count, with a flat charge covering the opening pages and a smaller one for every sheet after those.
  • A mortgage or deed of trust costs more than a deed, with a longer first stretch of pages.
  • Plats are priced per sheet and certified copies per page.
  • Filing the lender's release after payoff is free.
  • A page that breaks the state formatting rules picks up its own add-on charge.

Read the statute for the exact dollar figures. If your payoff is part of the sale, the free release means the lender's cleanup step will not cost you anything extra.

sections.h2: How does the Montgomery County tax office use what is recorded?
sections.html:
The Tax Administrator keeps the ownership and parcel records that begin with recorded deeds, then lists, values and bills each property. According to the county tax department page, the office oversees about 30,000 parcels of real property.

Which office sends your bill depends on the address. The county collects its own tax plus the real estate tax for Biscoe, Star, Candor and Mount Gilead. Troy collects for itself. Lake Tillery, Badin Lake and Wadeville fire district charges ride along on the county bill.

  • The county was last revalued in 2020, with the next reappraisal scheduled for 2028.
  • Commissioners adopt the rate in June, and the county mails bills in the summer after that.
  • The county says bills fall due September 1 and are not past due until January 5.
  • The listing window runs from January 2 to January 31, and listing late costs a 10% penalty.
  • The office can garnish wages, attach bank accounts, levy personal property, use debt setoff or foreclose on real estate to collect unpaid tax.

The state tax lien reaches the parcel on the listing date (G.S. 105-355), so request a payoff statement from the tax office or Troy before any fall or winter closing.

sections.h2: What if a Montgomery County deed is signed and left unrecorded?
sections.html:
A buyer holding an unrecorded deed is exposed. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance, an option or a lease running past three years gives no protection against creditors holding liens, or buyers who paid value, until it is entered in the land records of the parcel's own county.

Registration order sets priority. If a creditor records a judgment before the deed is filed, the creditor may win. Families sometimes keep a signed deed in a drawer for years, and that habit is the surest way to create the problem.

The cure is quick. Carry the signed, notarized deed in along with the excise payment and filing fee, and hold on to the recording details the staff give back.

sections.h2: What should a Montgomery County seller prepare before recording?
sections.html:
Most of the effort comes before anyone reaches the counter. Register of deeds staff in North Carolina record documents without drafting them or advising on them, so a lawyer prepares the deed.

  • Look up the parcel number and owner record on the county's real estate and GIS search so the deed's description matches the tax record.
  • Gather payoff letters for each mortgage or lien, and confirm each lender will file its release.
  • Find out whether the county or the Town of Troy collects the tax on your parcel.
  • Have the excise payment and the recording fee ready as separate amounts.
  • Keep the notarized original with the recording stamp once the deed is filed.

Call the Montgomery County Register of Deeds for current hours and ask how it accepts documents before you make the trip.

sections.h2: Which other Montgomery County offices touch a home sale?
sections.html:
The register of deeds is one stop among several. The county's department list includes Inspections, Planning, Environmental Health, Public Utilities, Veteran Services and the Tax Department, and each can come up during a sale.

  • Inspections and the building permit desk answer questions about unpermitted work a buyer may spot.
  • Planning covers lot size and setback questions for parcels in the unincorporated area.
  • Environmental Health is where well and septic questions land on rural lots.
  • Public Utilities and the online water bill page help the buyer move the account.
  • The county runs a program to enroll farmland in a voluntary agricultural district, and an enrolled parcel carries that status into the sale.

The county's website also has a how-do-I menu with a real estate and GIS search, a permit link and an occupancy tax payment link. Starting there often saves a phone call.

faqs.q: Which party owes the Montgomery County excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. The transferor pays the county office ahead of filing, at $1.00 per $500 block of value.

faqs.q: Where is the price list for recording in Montgomery County?
faqs.a: Read G.S. 161-10, the one price list that every North Carolina register of deeds follows. Pages drive the charge for a deed, a mortgage costs more, and a release after payoff is free.

faqs.q: Will the office draft my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. Staff file deeds but do not write them or offer legal advice. A closing attorney or other lawyer prepares the deed, and the office records it after it is signed and notarized.

faqs.q: When is a Montgomery County tax bill late?
faqs.a: The county lists September 1 as the due date and January 5 as the point where a bill is past due. Interest then starts at 2%, and each month from February adds another 3/4 of 1%.

faqs.q: Does the county collect tax on a house inside Troy?
faqs.a: Troy collects its own real estate tax. The county office handles the county bill plus the bills for Biscoe, Star, Candor and Mount Gilead, so a Troy owner can expect a town bill and a county bill.
